argument_summary: The present record does not support clean certification on rollout controls alone. It does support a narrower position: aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout is staged and reversible, and public governance guidance supports monitored deployment, but the exposed clinical coding assistant weakness triggers a specific prelaunch disclosure duty. The supportable defense is therefore conditional certification only if launch approval is explicitly tied to including that limitation in the launch model card. That narrows the Actor's claim to a caveated path rather than an unconditional one.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation beyond a bounded caveat would impose delay despite admissible evidence that the launch is otherwise near readiness, has no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and includes staged rollout and rollback controls. A caveated treatment preserves governance discipline without overstating the gap as a basis for broader launch stoppage.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy is the release-record predicate, not the general monitoring principles. That policy says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is approved risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The admissible record shows neither exclusion nor approved risk acceptance for the exposed clinical coding assistant segment. It also says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, the only supportable certification theory is one conditioned on launch-time disclosure of the known limitation; monitoring and rollback support that path but do not independently satisfy the policy.
concessions: The current record does not contain the actual launch model card or another admissible artifact proving the required disclosure will appear at launch.
The current record does not contain approved risk acceptance covering the exposed clinical coding assistant limitation.
The affected clinical coding assistant segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls alone are not sufficient under policy.
Clean present compliance is not supportable on the existing admissible record.
